questions.question: In cricket, when a ball bowled as per rules passes the batsman without touching the bat or batsman and runs are scored on that ball, then those runs are considered as ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bye**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bye**: A run is scored when the batsman does not touch the ball with either his bat or body. First recorded in the 1770s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**A** glossary of cricket terms**:

 
 

 **Terms**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

questions.question: Which of the given colours in NOT associated with the judo grades?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pink**__.

__
 
• **Judo belt colors** generally include white, yellow, orange, green, blue, brown, and black.
 
• The color **pink** is not traditionally associated with judo grades.
 
• Judo belts signify the rank and expertise level of the practitioner, with **white** being the beginner level and **black** representing advanced proficiency.
 
• Some variations in belt colors can exist between different judo organizations, but pink is not a standard color.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The judo ranking system is based on the Kyu-Dan system, where Kyu grades are for colored belts and Dan grades are for black belts.
 
• Each color indicates the level of knowledge and proficiency in judo techniques.
 
 
 
• **Origin of Judo:**
 
 
• Judo was created by Jigoro Kano in Japan in 1882.
 
• Kano developed judo as a physical, mental, and moral pedagogy in the form of a martial art.
 
 
 
• **Judo in the Olympics:**
 
 
• Judo was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.
 
• It is a globally practiced sport with significant international competitions.
 
 
 
• **Judo Techniques:**
 
 
• Judo techniques are classified into throwing techniques (nage-waza) and grappling techniques (katame-waza).
 
• Mastery of these techniques is essential for advancement in judo ranks.
